device_message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity of one logical to-device message. Queue services MUST preserve it byte-for-byte across retries and redelivery. Receivers deduplicate by the exact closed sender identity and device_message_id: (sender_account_id, sender_device_id, device_message_id), (sender_agent_id, device_message_id), or (sender_id, device_message_id).

sender_account_id.description: Exact cross-Station sender AccountId for the human-device branch. It is paired with sender_device_id and verified against that exact Account's accepted PCR device projection; it is forbidden in Agent and Station branches.

sender_device_id.description: Authoring human device. Exactly one sender endpoint branch is present: sender_account_id plus this field, the complete sender_agent_* triple, or sender_id. An Agent runtime has no device identity and MUST NOT be disguised as an ak:device; the restricted Station materializer likewise has a service identity rather than a fake device.

sender_agent_id.description: Agent principal that authored this message. Present exactly when the sender is an Agent runtime, together with sender_agent_verification_method and sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id. It is the sole Agent identity carrier.

sender_agent_verification_method.description: Verification method the Agent currently signs with. The device branch gets the equivalent from the accepted device projection; without this the receiver would hold an Agent principal id and no way to say which key speaks for it.

sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted Agent key authorization Event that anchors sender_agent_verification_method.

sender_id.description: Station service identity that internally materialized an actor-private update for the holder. This branch is restricted to actor_private_update_kind, and sender_id MUST equal recipient_account_id.station_id and the Station identity bound to the recipient's current authenticated self/to-device surface. It is not a bearer delegation and cannot be submitted through ak.self.device_messages.command.send.v1.

recipient_account_id.description: Exact cross-Station recipient AccountId. Pair with recipient_device_id for targeted delivery; the envelope MUST be rejected when either AccountId component or the device differs from the authenticated queue binding.

unsigned.description: Optional non-authenticated metadata block (transport-layer hints only). Receivers MUST NOT trust any field here for authorization, ordering, or cryptographic verification. Typical sub-fields: progress (delivery progress hint), error_context (transport-layer error diagnostics), retry_after_ms. By convention this block is excluded from the signed transcript of the enclosing transport envelope and is dropped on persist.

allOf.$comment: Closed sender endpoint XOR: sender_account_id plus sender_device_id, the complete sender_agent_* triple, or sender_id. Half-filled and mixed branches are rejected.

Only the recipient Station's internal materializer may use the service branch, and only for the closed actor-private update kind set. sender_id equality with recipient_account_id.station_id and authenticated service binding are semantic checks described by the normative prose.

actor_private_update_kind.description: Closed DeviceMessageEnvelope.kind set for actor-private sibling-device projection updates. These values are transport discriminators, not Event kinds and never enter shared Realm history.

secret_request_content.description: ak.secret.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.2). A newly authorized device asks an existing authorized device to hand over an account-scope secret over HPKE. Carries no secret material itself.

request_id.description: Caller-generated random correlation id; MUST NOT be reused after the request is answered or cancelled.

secret_id.description: Opaque identifier of the requested secret, e.g. example_mls_account_secret.

from_device_id.description: Requesting (new) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: base64url X25519 HPKE public key the requesting device controls and the responder seals to. It MUST be byte-identical to the hpke_key registered for from_device in the current accepted device projection. A responder MUST fail closed on any mismatch and MUST NOT accept an ephemeral key merely because it appeared in some other transcript; a verification checkpoint binds the device signing key and the accepted hpke_key, never an unverified sealing key.

read_cursor_update_content.description: ak.read_cursor.update actor-private sibling-device content (read-receipts.md §6.6 step 2). A derived projection of the ak.read_cursor.advance Event that currently wins the causal-first merge for one (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope); it is NOT the ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 payload object (which has no id and no updated_at) and never enters shared Realm history. updated_at is the winning advance Event envelope created_at.

actor_id.description: Holder whose read position advanced; MUST equal the recipient principal of the enclosing envelope.

device_id.description: Device that authored the winning advance.

updated_at.description: Envelope created_at of the winning ak.read_cursor.advance Event; derived, never a payload field.

secret_send_content.description: ak.secret.send to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.2). The existing authorized device returns the requested secret HPKE-sealed to the requester's recipient_hpke_public_key. The plaintext is never visible to the queue service.

request_id.description: Correlates to the pending ak.secret.request; MUST equal the request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD. Receivers MUST drop sends that do not match a locally pending request_id.

secret_id.description: Opaque requested secret identifier; MUST equal the secret_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD.

from_device_id.description: Authorizing (existing) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id and MUST be a non-revoked device of the recipient principal.

ciphertext.description: base64url HPKE AEAD ciphertext over the secret plaintext. The plaintext MUST carry the requested secret body, version, request_id and secret_id. For this human-device-only secret branch, the HPKE AAD is the RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of {device_message_id, kind, sender_account_id, sender_device_id, recipient_account_id, recipient_device_id, request_id, secret_id, expires_at}; both AccountId objects are covered in full. expires_at is the exact already-validated canonical Arkret UTC millisecond string from DeviceMessageEnvelope and MUST NOT be converted to a second epoch field. Freshness for server-assigned sent_at is bound by the sender-assigned device_message_id plus the one-time request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and AAD.
